author: franc464
text:
I'm not an expert at all, but agree with Rinehart.

author: Rinehart
text:
staurum wrote: Yes, that is part of emotional/psychology practice.

Knowing where to net BE vs being confident in a trade for a big R / home run.

Here s another loss

If you are having trouble with the emotions of taking some profit, why
not make it mechanical. Take 1/2 partial profit at 1:1 no matter what,
so if you leave your original SL you are net BE. Because frankly, these
 examples show trades running 2:1, 3:1, 4:1 into profit and still
getting closed for a loss.

You are a very good RTM trader. However, you cannot expect all trades to work every time so you must protect your capital.

author: staurum
text:
Yes, understood. Greed & Fear of missing profit / slow growth is poisonous.

3:1 1%R

If run perfectly, Potential Loss = 1%, Potential Reward = 3%.

If taken at 1R, Potential Loss = 1% to 0% (break-even), Potential Reward = 2%.

Of course, every situation will vary depending on PA given at any given time & circumstances.

Looking forward to what could've been done to foresee a trade may turn into a loss and therefore exit early.

:)
